name: AAWA: Saturday Night Fight

matches.finish: Synapse defeated Power Warrior with a Full Nelson slam ("The Cure") in 13:17.
The Vampyre defeated Voodoo with a DDT ("The Embrace") in 15:43.
"Excellence" Jeff Easthope defeated "Rowdy" Ryan by reversing a Crossbody Press into a pin.

matches.title: aawa-1997-world
matches.finish: Rip Daddy Scorpio defeated Death Demon with a top-rope legdrop ("Rip Daddy Suicide") in 15:56 to retain the title.

notes: The premiere edition of the AAWA's weekly 'Saturday Night Fight' -- one of the two named weekly shows the wing's own registry flagged as unstructured. All four matches are wholly AAWA-internal and are structured above. Two managers (Xrys, accompanying Synapse; Arlan Oanes, accompanying Power Warrior) appear on-air but are not minted from a single walk-in mention. Read in full.

name: AAWA Special Event: Battle Royale....Part Deux
notes: A 25-entrant, two-winner battle royal qualifying the AAWA's own representatives for an inter-federation 'E-Cup' tournament, run as a cross-promotional supercard with a rival fed, the CWO (the transcript's own commentary places several entrants, including both eventual winners, The Focus and Dakota Bundy, as CWO regulars: "They know each other's weaknesses... in the CWO"). Not structured into matches[]: of the 25 billed entrants, only the seven listed in appearances[] above are AAWA's own already-minted roster; the rest are either the CWO's own wrestlers (canonical-copy: their own wing's material, not reproduced here) or unminted for this wing, so per the wing's own convention an opponent not on this wing's own roster stays out of the structured record and the bout lives in the served page's own text. The two winners (The Focus, Dakota Bundy) are not minted. Read in full (this post is itself a follow-up correcting a truncated original post -- 'the final moments of the rumble didn't originally post due to the size of the event' -- and appears to be the complete result).

name: AAWA: Wicked Wednesday Wrestling (13 Aug 1997)

date.source: the fed's own post (msg_id obKX_0EsyFIJ/B8MNkvke5X8J), subject line 'Wicked Wednesday Wrestling ... (AAWA: 8-13)'

matches.finish: Thrown out: Green Goblin blinds Easthope with powder mid-match, and the blinded Easthope accidentally strikes the referee, drawing no decision.
Rip Daddy Scorpio defeated Synapse with a small package after Synapse hesitated to finish him off with a second piledriver.

notes: The first of four further dated 1997 'Wicked Wednesday Wrestling'/'W3' editions this pass structures. Opens (match order 1) with an unstructured six-man tag (Kurt Gerstung, Steve White and Tommy Bomber, billed as three members of 'the Army of Four,' beat Jensei Koshiro, Johnny Glide and Mr. Deathlock in 13:45) -- left out of matches[] because three of the six competitors (Bomber, Koshiro, Deathlock) are not otherwise minted from this pass's own single-appearance-each showing; Gerstung, White and Glide still carry appearances[] credit, and matches[] order numbering (2, 3) preserves this opener's own card position. 'Monster' Rich Clark appears only via a pre-recorded video insert rejecting a tag offer from Death Demon; he does not wrestle and is not minted. Read in full.

name: AAWA: 'W3' (19 Aug 1997)

date.source: the fed's own post (msg_id uW4HuMFBwGoJ), subject line "AAWA: 'W3' 8-19 2/2"

matches.finish: No-DQ/submission match: two unnamed Goblin-costumed impostors (referenced without individual names as 'Super and HobGoblin' in a later recap montage, msg_id 6hjN-xlnfYMJ) run in and help Green Goblin and Harry Osborne beat Easthope down before pinning him with the Goblin Glider in 15:46.
Rip Daddy Scorpio defeated Miguel Sanchez with a Frankensteiner.

notes: Held corpus carries only part 2 of 2 for this edition; part 1 does not survive in the wing's own tag partition. The two unnamed Goblin-costumed impostors who help beat Easthope down are never individually named or minted -- retroactively gestured at as 'Super and HobGoblin' in the 3 Sep recap montage (msg_id 6hjN-xlnfYMJ) but with no card of their own separating them. Sets up the 'September Sizzle' World Title match promised between Rip Daddy Scorpio and Green Goblin (not itself in this pass's own held corpus). Read in full.

name: AAWA: Wicked Wednesday Wrestling (27 Aug 1997)

date.source: the fed's own post (msg_id Pi3ogYeHRWYJ/c7ZHC_tXQ0wJ), subject lines "AAWA: 'Wicked Wednesday Wrestling' 8-27 1/2" and "AAWA: 'W3' 8-27 2/2"

matches.finish: Chris 'Predator' Moore defeated the debuting-week Johnny Glide with a free-falling piledriver ('The Prey') in 9:13, in Moore's own debut.
ColdFront (Steve White and Kurt Gerstung) defeated 'Rowdy' Ryan's newly-unveiled Iron and Steel in 15:35, Jimmy Heat's chair shot to Iron proving decisive.

Rip Daddy Scorpio defeated Jeff Easthope with a snapping belly-to-belly suplex, wrestling without his own World Heavyweight Championship belt after an off-screen theft recapped via video earlier in the broadcast (see that title's own reign note).

notes: Match order 3 on this card: Death Demon beat the CWO's own Television Champion, The Focus, in a cross-promotional singles match -- not structured into matches[] (The Focus belongs to a rival fed's own roster, canonical-copy rule, and is not minted here); matches[] order numbering (1, 2, 4) preserves this card position. The main event (order 4) closes with Scorpio clubbed unconscious backstage by an unseen attacker after his win. 'Rowdy' Ryan also cuts a promo (no match) unveiling his hired duo Iron and Steel and challenging Jimmy Heat, 'the Phantom' (not otherwise attested in this pass, not minted) and commentator Josh Miller to a Survivor Series-style match; that challenge is not resolved in this pass's own held corpus. Read in full.

name: AAWA: 'W3' (3 Sep 1997)

matches.finish: Miguel Sanchez defeated Chris 'Predator' Moore in a bloody 19:50 to retain -- unbilled as a title match -- his 'Master of Mayhem' championship.

notes: Held corpus carries only part 1 of 2 for this edition; part 2 does not survive in the wing's own tag partition, and this is the fed's own last-known-post date in the corpus overall. Match order 1: Dan Tucker upsets Steel in 9:32 in his own debut, then is beaten down after the bell by Steel, Iron and 'Rowdy' Ryan together -- not structured into matches[] because Tucker himself is not minted from a single appearance this pass, per the wing's own 2+-appearance mint threshold; Steel still carries appearances[] credit for the bout. Match order 2: Dragon Lee (accompanied by Mr. Ishihara) upsets Death Demon in 8:13 via a mist-assisted rollup, in Lee's own only appearance read this pass -- also below the mint threshold, also left out of matches[] (Demon keeps appearances[] credit). matches[] order numbering (3) preserves the surviving main event's own card position.
